# magpie

> magpie is a free, open-source (MIT) desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux that lets every AI coding agent use every model. Add a provider once (DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Qwen, MiniMax, OpenRouter, Ollama, or the Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions you already pay for), then pick it in Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI or any other agent. It runs a local gateway that speaks the OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini APIs and translates between them, with streaming, tool calls and reasoning intact.

magpie lives in the menu bar (tray on Windows and Linux), with a full window, a TUI and a CLI. The Mac download is about 15 MB, built on the system WebView (no Electron). It is signed and notarised on macOS and updates itself.

Key facts:

- Website: https://usemagpie.ai/ (English), https://usemagpie.ai/zh/ (中文), https://usemagpie.ai/ja/ (日本語), https://usemagpie.ai/de/ (Deutsch)
- Source code: https://github.com/yetone/magpie
- Downloads: https://github.com/yetone/magpie-releases/releases/latest
- Install from a terminal (macOS, Linux): `curl -fsSL https://usemagpie.ai/install.sh | sh`
- Community: Discord, linked from the website
- Price: free
- Full text of every docs page in one file: https://usemagpie.ai/llms-full.txt

This file holds the full text of every English docs page. The index is https://usemagpie.ai/llms.txt.

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/start

# Get started

magpie is one place to choose the model each of your agents uses. Add the providers you have, then pick a model per agent; magpie writes it into that agent’s own config.

Behind it is a small gateway on your machine, at `127.0.0.1:3425`. It speaks the OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini APIs and translates between them, streaming and tool calls included, so any agent can use any provider’s models: Claude Code on a GPT model from your ChatGPT plan, Codex on DeepSeek, OpenCode on your Claude plan.

### Providers

Where models come from: subscriptions you sign in to, vendors you have an API key for, and your own endpoints. Each model is named `provider/model`.

### Agents

The tools that use them: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and the rest. One row each, with the model it is set to.

### Gateway

The local endpoint every agent is pointed at when you pick a model through magpie. It sends each request to whoever serves that model.

### Routing groups

Optional. Several models or accounts an agent picks as one, `group/<id>`, for when one runs out of quota.

1. **Add providers.** Sign in to your subscriptions, paste API keys. Once is enough.
2. **Pick a model for each agent.** Click the agent’s model, choose one. magpie rewrites that agent’s config.
3. **Start a new session.** Agents read their config when they start; the next session uses the new model.

## 1 · Add your providers

Open the Providers tab and press ＋ Add provider. Pick a tile, or type a vendor’s name to find it.

### Subscriptions · sign in, no key

Claude (Pro, Max, Team), ChatGPT (Plus, Pro, Business), Copilot, Gemini (Code Assist) and Antigravity; Cursor, Grok (SuperGrok), Devin and others are added from the Plugins page. Click the tile and magpie opens the vendor’s own sign-in page in your browser; the account shows up as soon as you finish (Copilot gives you a code to enter on GitHub’s page). Subscriptions are added here, in magpie, not by logging in inside another agent.

- **More than one account..** Click the Claude or ChatGPT tile again to add another; each is listed under the provider, one click from being the one in use.
- **Already signed in?.** An agent you are signed in to on this machine shows up as a provider too, *signed in as …*.
- **Every agent can use it..** A subscription’s models are `claude/…`, `codex/…`, `copilot/…`, `antigravity/…` in every other agent’s picker: to run Antigravity’s Claude or Gemini models in Codex or Claude Code, sign in to Antigravity here and pick an `antigravity/…` model on the agent’s row. Nothing else to set up. Google may suspend an Antigravity account it sees used outside Antigravity, so use one you can afford to lose. Claude subscription requests run through the Claude Code installed on this machine, so keep it installed.

### Vendors

Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Kimi, Zhipu GLM, MiniMax, Qwen, Mistral, Groq, xAI and more. Pick one, paste the key (Get a key ↗ links to the vendor’s key page), save. magpie asks the vendor which models it serves and offers those; open the provider’s row to choose which ones agents see, or Test it.

### On this machine

Ollama and LM Studio. No key.

### Custom · any compatible URL

For anything else: a Name, an OpenAI compatible base URL (ending in `/v1`), an Anthropic compatible one (the root, what `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` would take), or both, and the key. Give every API the endpoint speaks; each agent uses the one it speaks natively and magpie translates for the rest.

> **Already set up providers in Claude Code or Codex?** Import… at the top of the sheet reads Claude Code’s `settings.json` and Codex’s `config.toml`, changes nothing in them, and brings over the providers you tick.

Keys live in `~/.config/magpie/providers.json`, readable by you alone. magpie never reads keys from your shell environment: what you add is what it uses.

## 2 · Pick a model for each agent

The Agents tab has a row for each agent installed or configured on this machine. magpie knows Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, MiMo Code, DevEco Code, Pi, Goose, Cursor CLI, Copilot CLI, Crush, DeepSeek Harness, Command Code, omp, OmO, Devin, Hermes Agent, MiniMax Code, Grok Build, ZCode, OpenHanako and Alma.

- **Click the model.** to open the picker. Models are grouped: the agent’s own, your routing groups, then each provider you added. Type to filter, or type any model id that is not listed.
- **Reasoning effort.** , where the agent has it (Codex’s *effort*, Pi’s *thinking*), is a slider under the list.
- **Fast mode..** A model with a fast mode has a bolt on its row, beside its star; it shows on the picked row and under the pointer. That is a GPT model of a ChatGPT (Codex) account, a GPT or o-series model on an OpenAI key, Cursor’s models with a fast variant, Claude Opus on an Anthropic key, and a plugin’s or another magpie’s model that says it is served at priority. Click it, and every request this agent sends that model goes in its vendor’s fast mode, quicker at a higher price: `service_tier: "priority"`, as Codex’s own `/fast` sends it, or Claude’s `speed: "fast"`, whatever API the agent speaks. Click again for Ultrafast, where a ChatGPT account offers it on the model, and again for the usual speed. Each agent is switched apart, and the model’s fallbacks go as they are. In a routing group, each member has the same switch in its row.
- **Claude Code through magpie.** can also give its opus, sonnet and haiku tiers models of their own; by default they follow the main model.

Picking a model writes it into the agent’s own config file. Only the keys magpie needs change; comments, ordering and indentation survive, and writes are atomic.

| Agent | What a model through magpie writes |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/settings.json`: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` and the model variables in its `env` block |
| Codex | `~/.codex/config.toml`: a `[model_providers.magpie]` table and the model, with the list in `magpie-models.json`. Your ChatGPT sign-in is left alone |
| OpenCode, MiMo Code, DevEco Code, Pi, Crush | A `magpie` provider entry, and `magpie/provider/model` |
| AtomCode | `~/.atomcode/config.toml`: a `magpie` provider account and one model entry per catalog model |
| Snow CLI | `~/.snow/profiles/magpie.json`: a `magpie` profile, made the active one (Snow App takes it in with "Sync Snow CLI API config") |
| QwenPaw | A `magpie` provider in `~/.qwenpaw.secret/providers/custom/magpie.json`, and each agent's `active_model` in its `agent.json`. Restart QwenPaw after the first connect |
| Gemini CLI | `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` pointed at the gateway, API-key auth, and the model |

**A running session keeps the model it started with.** Agents read their config when they start, so the change applies to the next session. Codex builds its model list at start-up too: restart the Codex app and open `codex` sessions after a switch.

> **Paseo, editor extensions and other front-ends** that run Claude Code or Codex for you start the same CLI, which reads the same `~/.claude` or `~/.codex` config. Set the model once in magpie and they get it too, from their next session.

> **`claude-magpie`: Claude Code through magpie, `claude` left as it is.** To keep a plain `claude` on your own Claude account and start magpie's Claude Code only when you ask for it, leave Claude Code unconnected and run `claude-magpie` instead. It starts the same `claude` with magpie's settings over yours for that session (the gateway, the model and its tiers), so `~/.claude/settings.json` is never rewritten. Every argument goes to Claude Code: `claude-magpie --resume`, `claude-magpie -p "…"`. magpie puts it beside the `magpie` command when you add that in Settings › Command line; with the command there already, run `magpie claude launcher add` once. `magpie claude run` does the same. A model you pick with `/model` in it is kept for the next `claude-magpie`, and your own `claude` keeps its model. magpie has to be running.

## 3 · Optional: routing groups

With one account per provider you can skip this. It matters once you have several: two ChatGPT accounts, or the same model from a subscription and from a key.

### Several accounts or keys in one provider

Open the provider’s row and tick every account or key to use. Routing says how requests spread over them: Smart (the default), In order, Until used up, staying on the next once one is used up even after the first renews, In turn, Least used first, Use before expiry, By weight, each account or key taking its share by the weight set beside it (a Max account 5, a Pro one 1), or Speed first, the key that answered fastest lately first. Fallback lists models to use instead when the provider is out of quota, rate limited or down.

### One model over several providers

A group is several models, from one provider or many, that an agent picks as one: `group/<id>`, under *Routing groups* in the picker. A model two of your providers serve under the same name becomes a group on its own; New group in the Routing tab makes one of any models you like. The first model answers for what the group can do.

> **Groups you get without doing anything.** Add a second provider that serves a model you already have — Claude Opus from your Claude subscription and from Copilot, DeepSeek from its own API and from OpenRouter — and magpie makes it a group by itself, `auto/<model>` (the model's own id, as in `auto/claude-opus-4.6`; the older `group/auto-…` id still works), over every provider that serves it. The name is matched however each vendor spells it (`deepseek/deepseek-chat`, `deepseek-chat`). Pick it for an agent to spread its requests over all of them; `magpie group rm` hides one you don’t want.

> **One model under the provider's odd id.** Some providers serve a model under an id of their own, `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` or `grok-4.6@500k`. Give it the id you want in the provider's editor, under Names, prices & levels, in Listed as beside Same as, then Save; or run `magpie model id relay/grok-4.6@500k grok-4.6`. magpie then lists it, routes it, joins it to the `auto/grok-4.6` group with your other providers' `grok-4.6`, holds gateway keys to it and counts its usage as `grok-4.6`, and still asks the provider for `grok-4.6@500k`. One id is one model of a provider: the last one you give it to has it, and the provider's own model of that id is left out of the list while it does. `magpie model id relay/grok-4.6 --reset` takes it back, and `magpie model ids` lists them. It works for a subscription you signed in to and a plugin's provider too (`magpie model id cursor/deepseek-v41-flash-1017 deepseek-v4.1-flash`): the account or the plugin is still asked for its own id.

| Routing | What goes first |
| --- | --- |
| Smart `smart` | The default. Over the members’ accounts and keys together (a group in the group as one, see below): of the subscriptions with quota to spare, the one whose allowance renews soonest. The week decides; an account with five hours and no week (Claude Enterprise) goes by its five hours, so ahead of every week renewing later. Credits with no reset (WorkBuddy’s packages, each ending on its own day) count as renewing when the soonest of those left run out, so the WorkBuddy account whose credits end first goes first; accounts renewing together (free ones at the month’s end) go by whose credits left end first after that. One resting after a failure goes last. |
| In order `order` | The first model until it can’t answer, then the next. |
| Until used up `drain` | One account or key until it is used up, then the next, which keeps the requests: one before it that renews meanwhile doesn’t take them back. One rate limited or failing is passed over only while it rests. |
| In turn `rotate` | Each conversation’s next turn goes to the next member’s account or key, spreading the load. |
| Least used `usage` | The account or key with the most of its allowance left. |
| Use before expiry `pace` | The account with the most of its week left per hour until it renews — the one with the most to lose at its reset — so less of each member’s week is lost at its reset; an account with five hours and no week (Claude Enterprise) by what its five hours have left per hour until they renew, so almost always first. Credits in an account that expire before it resets count too: those that expire first, per hour until they do, when that is the more (WorkBuddy’s check-in credits). One at 90% or more waits until the others can’t answer. A key by the tokens sent it lately. |
| By weight `weight` | Each model takes its share of the requests by the weight set beside it in the group editor (1 to 1000, 1 if unset): one weighing 3 takes three for every one a model weighing 1 takes, spread out rather than in bursts. Each model is tried whole over its own accounts or keys, as its provider routes them, and a group in the group counts as one. One resting after a failure leaves the round; the next model is the fallback when one fails. |
| Speed first `fast` | The member, account or key that answered this model fastest lately: the time to its first token and how fast it writes, newer answers counting more. Those within a tenth of each other keep their order. One not measured in the last hour gets one request in five, so a channel that was slow once is tried again; one resting after a failure goes last. Only streamed replies are measured, and a restart measures again from scratch. |
| Cheapest first `cheap` | Groups only. The member whose model costs least now, by its price a million tokens in and out at this hour as Usage counts it: your own price for it, else its list price, at the provider’s price rate and rate windows. DeepSeek’s own API, Command Code’s and OpenCode Go’s DeepSeek models cost double in their peak hours (weekdays 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC), and Ollama Cloud’s DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and V4 Pro in its own (weekdays 12:00–18:00 UTC, half price the rest of the time), so a DeepSeek model listed on two providers goes to the one cheaper at that hour. Members that cost the same keep their order; one with no known price goes last. |

| Stays | How long a conversation stays with the account or key that answered it |
| --- | --- |
| Auto `auto` | The default. Within a turn always, across turns while what the vendor cached of it is worth keeping. |
| Session `session` | The whole session, while it can answer. With Smart, Least used first or Use before expiry, a new session goes to the account or key the fewest other sessions are on, so sessions side by side each keep one of their own. |
| Within a turn `turn` | While the agent sends tool results back; when you speak again, routing decides afresh. |
| Off `off` | Every request is routed afresh. |
| Strict `strict` | Never moves to another account or key, even past its usage cap: when that one is rate limited or out of quota, the error goes to the agent. New conversations are spread as with Session. |

### Rules · a turn to a chosen model

A group’s Rules send a turn to one of its models when the turn is of a kind you name: long (`tokens ≥ N`), carrying an image, asking for reasoning (on, or at least a level), from certain agents, asking for something you describe (an *intent*), the agent compacting its context, or working in one of some folders (a project). A rule’s conditions all have to hold, so one can say “in ~/work/acme, and long”. They are looked at top first when you send a message; the first that matches puts its model first, with the group’s others behind it if it fails. A turn no rule matches is routed as the group always routes, and keeps to where it was.

- A rule decides as a turn begins, and the turn stays on that model while the agent sends tool results back, so what the vendor cached isn’t lost halfway. The one exception: a turn that grows past its model’s context moves to a member that takes it.
- Tokens are estimated from the request’s size, or what the vendor counted for the conversation’s last request, whichever is more. Leave some margin: a rule at 150k for a 200k model, not 199k.
- A subagent is a conversation of its own, so a rule can send it elsewhere while its agent keeps where it is.
- An intent is a few words for what the user asks for — “writing or fixing tests”, “a quick question”. As a turn begins, the group’s classifier — any model magpie has; a small, fast one without reasoning is best — is asked once which of the intents that could match the user’s message is. Only the message is sent, not the conversation. If it fails, exceeds the configured timeout (8 s by default; set in Settings → Models → Replies → Intent classifier timeout) or can’t say, no intent matches and the turn goes by the other rules. It isn’t asked when a rule without an intent would decide anyway, and the same message isn’t asked about twice. Its calls show in Usage as magpie’s own. Exactly what it is asked, how its answer is used and what happens when it fails: [Intent routing](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/intent).
- compacting matches an agent compacting its conversation — Claude Code’s `/compact` and auto-compact, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Kimi Code — so a cheaper, faster model writes the summary while the conversation stays on its own. A compaction is decided on its own: the turn it happens in, and its cache, stay where they were. When the conversation is longer than the rule’s model takes, the next rule that matches, or the group’s order, decides instead.
- **Hours and days..** A rule can hold only at some hours, on some days, by this computer’s clock — a vendor’s peak hours, say. A rule that sends those turns elsewhere still leaves the vendor’s model behind it for failover. To keep a model out entirely, choose Pause the model instead from the rule’s ⋯ menu: while it holds (its hours and days, its agents), that model is left out of the group — never first, never a fallback, not kept for the conversation it was in — and it is back once they end. A pause holds by hours, days and agents only; if every model of the group is paused, the agent is told so.
- **Folders..** in folder matches a turn from an agent working in one of the folders you list, or a folder inside one: `~/work/acme` takes `~/work/acme/web`, not `~/work/acme-old`. The folder is the one the agent tells its model in the request — Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi say it — so an agent that doesn’t say its folder matches no folder rule. `~` is your home folder, `C:\work` is also WSL’s `/mnt/c/work`, and on macOS and Windows case doesn’t count.
- **Reasoning..** A rule can also set the reasoning its model is asked for, so an intent picks the model and the effort as a pair: Set its reasoning in the rule’s ⋯ menu, or `use-effort=low` from a terminal. The model is asked for it whatever the agent asked, at the model’s nearest level; a model whose levels magpie doesn’t know, and the models behind it for failover, are asked as the agent asked. See [Intent routing](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/intent#effort).
- The Routing tab says which rule sent each turn where, what the classifier said, and the folder the agent said it was in.

### Groups in groups

A group’s models can include another group: pick it under *Routing groups* in Add a model, or `models+=group/<id>` from a terminal. The group in it takes its place in the order and routes among its own models by its own routing and rules. So Coder can be `deepseek-v4-pro` then *Fast*, and Fast its own order of cheap models. A Coder rule can send a turn to `group/fast`, and Fast’s own rules then pick which of its models goes first.

- **No loops..** A group can’t be in itself, directly or through the groups in it. Saving Fast with Coder in it, while Coder has Fast, is refused, and the picker doesn’t offer such a group. Groups go at most 8 deep. A group can’t be removed while another has it: take it out there first.
- **Each group routes by its own routing..** Whatever the outer group’s routing, it never reaches inside a group in it: Smart, In turn, Least used or Use before expiry weighs the inner group as one member, by the account or key the inner group would try first, and where it lands the inner group is tried whole, in its own order. Coder on Smart with Claude (In order) and GPT (In order) in it compares Claude’s first with GPT’s first, not all of their accounts together.
- **So does a provider routed its own way..** A model whose provider routes its accounts or keys In order, In turn, by Least used, Use before expiry or Weight keeps that inside any group, weighed as one by the account or key it would try first and tried whole in its own order. One left on Smart, the default, has its accounts weighed with the group’s others as one pool, so the one whose allowance renews soonest goes first whichever provider it is of.
- **Failover goes through..** If every model in the inner group fails, the outer group’s next member answers, as with any member.
- A model that appears twice (on its own and in a group in it) is asked once, at its first place.

The Routing tab shows the gateway’s decisions live: who answered each request, and why. The same groups from a terminal:

```
magpie groups                        # yours, then those magpie found
magpie group add "Opus anywhere" models=claude/claude-opus-5-5,copilot/claude-opus-5.5 routing=order stays=session
magpie group set opus-anywhere models+=openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5
magpie group set opus-anywhere routing=weight weight=claude/claude-opus-5-5=3  # three of every four requests to it
magpie group rule add opus-anywhere use=openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 tokens=150k  # long turns to it first
magpie group rule add opus-anywhere use=copilot/claude-opus-5.5 intent="a quick question" classifier=groq/llama-3.1-8b-instant
magpie group rule add opus-anywhere use=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash compact  # /compact summaries to a cheap model
magpie group rule add opus-anywhere use=kimi/kimi-k2.6 folders=~/oss,"~/My Project"  # turns in those projects to it first
magpie group rule add opus-anywhere pause=copilot/claude-opus-5.5 time=14:00-18:00 days=mon-fri  # left out in those hours
magpie group rule add opus-anywhere pause=claude/claude-opus-5-5 except-folders=~/big-task  # the model kept for the task in ~/big-task: left out of every other folder
magpie group rule add opus-anywhere use=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash when="effort is off" when="not subagent"  # reasoning off, not a subagent
magpie group rule add opus-anywhere use=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash when="system matches ^你是对话标题命名"  # a harness's title call, told by its system prompt
magpie group set coder models+=group/opus-anywhere  # a group in a group
magpie group rule opus-anywhere      # its rules; rule rm|mv <n>, rule classifier <group> <model>
magpie group copy opus-anywhere "Opus test"  # the same models, routing and rules, to change on its own
magpie group rm opus-anywhere        # one magpie found is hidden; magpie group restore <id>
magpie claude group/opus-anywhere    # use it
```

## Usage and profiles

**Usage.** The Usage tab counts tokens, cache hits and cost for each agent and model, from every call through the gateway, for Today, 7 days, 30 days or All; your subscriptions’ allowance used, and when it resets, sits on top. Calls an agent makes to its own vendor directly don’t pass through magpie and aren’t counted.

**Context.** Usage’s Context tab shows what each agent’s prompts hold, read as they pass through the gateway: its system prompt, tool definitions (an MCP server’s as one), instruction files and skills, the files its tools read, their other output and the conversation, as parts of the model’s context window. Each agent gets a score out of 100 — how much of its prompt the cache reads, how lean it starts, how fast it fills and how often it fails — and tags such as *Lean start* or *MCP-heavy* that say what the score was told by. Open a session to see its latest request’s window, cell by cell; the Routing page shows the same for any request you pick. Click a part, a cell or an item to read its text as magpie sent it, masked where masking is on. That text is kept for the last 10 requests only, in memory while magpie runs; what is saved keeps names only, never your prompt’s text, and nothing of it is sent anywhere.

**Profiles.** At the bottom of the Agents tab, ＋ Save current snapshots every agent’s settings under a name; click the chip to switch everything back in one move. The profile in use is ticked, and the tray panel’s Profiles button shows its name; a setting changed by hand since clears the tick.

## From the terminal

`magpie tui` is the whole app in a terminal, and every step above has a command. `magpie help` lists them all.

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `magpie ls` | Every agent found and its settings |
| `magpie presets` | The vendors magpie knows |
| `magpie provider add deepseek sk-…` | Add a preset with its key |
| `magpie accounts add codex` | Sign in to one more Claude or ChatGPT subscription |
| `magpie accounts switch claude next` | Sign Claude Code (or `codex`) in to the next of your accounts that has room, or the one with the most left when none has |
| `magpie accounts discovery off` | Never read your agents’ sign-ins (Claude Code’s and Codex’s files, the Keychain); `on` reads them again |
| `magpie providers` | Your providers: host, key, models, who uses them |
| `magpie models` | Every model agents can pick, as `provider/model` |
| `magpie claude codex/gpt-5.5` | Set an agent’s model |
| `claude-magpie` | Claude Code through magpie for one session, a plain `claude` left on your account (`magpie claude run`; `magpie claude launcher add` puts it on PATH) |
| `magpie codex effort high` | Set another field |
| `magpie codex default` | Back to the agent’s own default, magpie’s wiring removed |
| `magpie save work` · `use work` | Save and apply a profile |
| `magpie usage 7d` | Tokens and cost per agent and model |
| `magpie tools` · `magpie tool generate_image "…" -o hero.png` | The tools magpie gives agents over MCP (image generation, image recognition, web search, plugins’), listed and called directly; an image it makes is saved |
| `magpie tray` | Start with the menu bar icon only |
| `magpie log` · `magpie log -f` | Where magpie’s logs are, to send with a report; `-n 200` prints the app log’s last lines, `-f` follows it |

## FAQ

### Do I need to export `OPENAI_BASE_URL` or `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`?

No. For the agents magpie lists, it writes the gateway’s address and token into the agent’s own config file. Those variables are only for other tools with a base-URL setting: the Gateway tab’s Connect section has them as copy buttons and snippets.

### Does magpie have to be running?

For a model through magpie, yes: the gateway runs with the app. Closing the window leaves it running in the menu bar or tray; `magpie tray` starts the icon alone (put it in your login items), and `magpie serve` runs just the gateway, and `magpie daemon install` keeps it running as a service (systemd on Linux, launchd on the Mac), from login or boot, with no window; `magpie daemon install --web` has it serve the browser page too, and `magpie daemon status` prints the page’s link. An agent on its own model and its own sign-in doesn’t go through magpie.

### How do I put an agent back the way it was?

Pick one of the agent’s own models in the picker, or run `magpie <agent> default`. magpie removes what it wrote and restores the values it replaced, such as an `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` you had before.

### I switched models, but my agent still uses the old one.

A running session keeps what it started with. Start a new one; for Codex, restart the Codex app too.

### Does editing the agent’s config by hand break anything?

No. magpie reads the files each time and touches only the keys it sets, so your other settings and comments stay. Providers brought over with Import… are copies: later changes in the agent’s settings aren’t copied again.

### Installing or updating behind a firewall, or without access to GitHub?

Give the installer and `magpie update` a proxy: `curl -fsSL https://usemagpie.ai/install.sh | sh -s -- --proxy http://127.0.0.1:7890`, or `magpie update --proxy socks5://127.0.0.1:1080` (http, https, socks5 and socks5h; `HTTPS_PROXY` and `ALL_PROXY` are honoured too). Release files come from usemagpie.ai (Cloudflare R2), and from github.com when that fails. `--mirror <prefix>` fetches the release file from a GitHub download mirror you choose, as `<prefix>https://github.com/…`, when the site’s copy fails; `magpie update mirror <prefix>` keeps it for every update, the app’s too, and `magpie update mirror off` removes it. No mirror is used unless you give one, and the file’s SHA-256 still comes from usemagpie.ai, never from the mirror: a file the mirror changed is refused. The app’s own updates go through Settings → Proxy.

### Which build does the installer put on Linux?

The desktop app (window, tray icon and a menu entry) when GTK 3 and WebKitGTK 4.1 are installed. On a computer with a desktop but without them, the installer installs WebKitGTK 4.1 with your package manager (apt, dnf, pacman or zypper), through `sudo`, which asks for your password, and then the app; it says what it installs before it asks. Run without a terminal (CI, a Dockerfile), without `sudo`, on another distribution or when that install fails, it installs the terminal build (`magpie tui`, `magpie web` and the CLI) and ends with the command that installs them, such as `sudo apt install libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0` on Debian and Ubuntu or `sudo dnf install webkit2gtk4.1` on Fedora; run the installer again afterwards for the app. A desktop counts whether you run it there or over ssh: a graphical session, your graphical login, or a desktop installed to log in to. A server without one gets the terminal build. To choose yourself, add `--gui` (the app even when its libraries can't be installed now) or `--tui` (the terminal build, and no package installed): `curl -fsSL https://usemagpie.ai/install.sh | sh -s -- --tui`.

### How do I uninstall magpie?

Installed with the script: `curl -fsSL https://usemagpie.ai/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall` has magpie disconnect every agent and put back what each had first, then takes off what the script put there: the `magpie` command, and the app on macOS or its menu entry, icon and `magpie://` handler on Linux, with magpie’s service and opening at login there, which would start a magpie that is gone. Your settings, providers and usage in `~/.config/magpie` stay, for when you install again. Add `--purge` to delete them too (`magpie uninstall --yes`). Installed another way, `magpie uninstall` or Settings → Uninstall magpie does what `--purge` does and leaves the program itself for you to delete.

Deleted magpie already (the app in the Trash, the folder removed) and an agent still says it can’t connect? On macOS and Linux run the same `--uninstall` line: with no magpie left it downloads the newest to a temporary folder, checked like an install, and that one puts your agents back while magpie’s record of what each had is still in `~/.config/magpie`. On Windows, download magpie again and use Settings → Uninstall magpie. To put Codex back by hand, quit it, then in `~/.codex/config.toml` delete each line under a `# magpie:` comment (`openai_base_url`, `model_provider = "magpie"`, `model_catalog_json`) and set `model` to one of Codex’s own; the `[model_providers.magpie]` table can go too once no thread you keep was started on magpie. Delete `~/.codex/magpie-models.json`, and open Codex again.

### Can magpie keep its files on another disk, so reinstalling the system doesn’t lose them?

Installed, magpie keeps its settings, providers, usage and library in `~/.config/magpie` (`C:\Users\<you>\.config\magpie` on Windows). It backs them up by itself once a day, into `auto-backups` in that same folder, so a reinstalled system loses the backups too; Settings → Sync and backup says so under Backup folder. Click Change… there and pick a folder on another disk (`D:\magpie-backups`) or one a cloud drive syncs. After a reinstall, install magpie, pick the same folder there and Restore… the newest version. Backups hold no API keys; Sign-ins in backups adds subscription accounts and plugin sign-ins, sealed with a passphrase. To carry the keys too, sync to a WebDAV folder, an S3 bucket or a GitHub repository, sealed with a passphrase, in the same place.

To keep magpie’s own files on that disk (an external SSD, say), click Move… beside Data folder in the same place and pick a folder there. magpie restarts, moves its files and cache into a folder named `magpie` inside it, and leaves a link where they were, so nothing else changes. Keep the disk connected: without it magpie won’t open until it is back. Move back brings them home. `magpie data move <folder>` does the same from a terminal.

To keep everything on that disk, run magpie portable: put `magpie.exe` in a folder there with an empty folder named `data` beside it (`D:\magpie\magpie.exe` and `D:\magpie\data`). magpie then keeps everything in `data`, its caches and log too, and writes nothing of its own to your user folder; Settings → About → Config folder says Portable. Open it, and restore a backup into it as above. After a reinstall, open `D:\magpie\magpie.exe` again. The agents’ own configs (`~/.claude`, `~/.codex`…) stay where each agent reads them.

### Where is magpie’s log?

The app (its window, the menu bar or tray icon and the panel, however it was opened) writes `app.log`: `~/Library/Logs/magpie/app.log` on macOS, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\magpie\logs\app.log` on Windows, `~/.local/state/magpie/app.log` on Linux (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/magpie` when that is set), and `logs` in a portable magpie’s data folder. Settings → About → Log has its path and an Open that shows its folder; `magpie log` prints it, and `magpie log -f` follows it. At 5 MiB it becomes `app.old.log` beside it, so two files at most are kept. It holds what magpie did and the errors it met (a provider refusing a request, a retry, a plugin that failed to start), not your keys, prompts or replies; what looks like a key or token is masked anyway. `magpie serve` run as a service logs elsewhere: `~/Library/Logs/magpie/serve.log` on macOS, `journalctl --user -u magpie` on Linux; `magpie log` names it too.

### What does magpie send about me?

Your prompts, replies, keys and accounts go only to the providers you use; magpie has no server of its own in the path. Once a day a released magpie tells us it is in use, so we know how many people use it and what to look after first: a random id made up on your computer, magpie’s version and your system, and which agents, providers and models it is used with, by magpie’s own ids (`claude`, `deepseek`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4`) with how many of each. A provider you added yourself, and a model on it, is only `custom`. For each partner listed first in the add sheet, how many times a day it was shown, opened and added from goes with them, as counts only. No names, base URLs, accounts, keys, prompts or usage are sent. Settings → Privacy → Share the agents, providers, models and plugins I use leaves out the agents, providers and models, the partner counts and which of Discover’s plugins are installed (for its counts of who uses and likes each); Count me as a user, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` or `MAGPIE_NO_STATS=1` turns it all off. Builds from source never send it. A partner's website and key-page links go through `usemagpie.ai/go/…`, which counts the click (the partner, which link, and a country) before sending you on, and usemagpie.ai counts how many times the partner list is fetched. The server sees these whatever the settings say, as any website sees its visits; no id, address or account is kept with them. Icons named by a plugin, an import link or the library are fetched through `usemagpie.ai/api/icon`, so their hosts see Cloudflare's address, not yours; the server only passes the picture on, and counts and keeps nothing. The [Privacy page](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/privacy) lists everything magpie sends by itself, with an example of the daily count, the files it keeps and every switch.

### The agent gets 502 or can’t connect, and nothing shows in magpie’s Routing tab?

A proxy app (Surge, Clash, mihomo and the like, with system proxy, TUN or enhanced mode on) has taken the agent’s request to `http://127.0.0.1:3425` and sent it somewhere else, so it never reaches magpie. The bypass list (`skip-proxy`, “bypass”) isn’t always enough: some agents, Codex among them, send it through the proxy anyway. Add rules that send the local addresses direct, ahead of your other rules:

```
IP-CIDR,127.0.0.0/8,DIRECT,no-resolve
IP-CIDR6,::1/128,DIRECT,no-resolve
```

In a Clash or mihomo config the same lines go under `rules:`, each starting with `- `. Then send the agent a new request.

### Can DeepSeek Harness keep its own DeepSeek row and go through magpie?

Yes, by hand. Connecting dsh adds magpie’s routes and leaves dsh’s DeepSeek row (`llm-deepseek`) to dsh. That row keeps DeepSeek’s cache when dsh’s prompt or tools change mid-session. To send it through magpie, add this to `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`:

```
- id: llm-deepseek
  config:
    baseURL: http://127.0.0.1:3425
    apiKeyEnv: MAGPIE_DS_KEY
    maxInlineRequestImageBytes: 67108864
    models:
      - id: deepseek/deepseek-flash
        name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (magpie)
        contextWindow: 1000000
        inputModalities: [text, image]
        systemPromptUpdate: in-history
        toolUpdate: addition-only
      - id: deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
        name: DeepSeek V4 Pro (magpie)
        contextWindow: 1000000
```

`baseURL` has no `/anthropic`. The model ids are magpie’s (`magpie models`), and a `models` list replaces dsh’s defaults, so keep the two update lines. `MAGPIE_DS_KEY` holds the gateway key (`magpie` on this computer), not your DeepSeek key: export it, put it in `~/.dsh/.env`, or enter it on the DeepSeek row in dsh’s Models page. Pick the model in dsh; Disconnect leaves the entry alone. magpie has no Files API, so dsh sends images inline as base64 each turn, up to `maxInlineRequestImageBytes` (20 MiB by default, 64 MiB above). Keep the row on DeepSeek’s own models. [More in the reference](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/main/docs/reference.md#deepseek-harness-the-deepseek-row-by-hand).

### Can Trae or Trae CN use magpie’s models?

Users report that this works. Trae keeps custom models in your Trae account, on its servers, so magpie can’t set it up for you, and Trae may not reach `127.0.0.1`. So:

1. In magpie, turn on Settings → Network and sharing → Share on local network, and note the Address it shows.
2. Take a gateway key (Gateway → Gateway keys, or `magpie gateway-key add "Trae"`).
3. In Trae’s custom model settings, enter that address as the address and the gateway key as the API key.

The model id is magpie’s (`magpie models`). Sharing lets other computers on your network in with a gateway key; see [Remote magpie](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/remote#share).

An error from the gateway? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting). Stuck, or have a setup worth sharing? Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF). Vendors who want to hand their users a ready-made provider: see [Add to magpie](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/import).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models

# Use DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Qwen or any model in Claude Code

Claude Code speaks one API, Anthropic Messages. magpie puts a gateway on your computer that speaks it for every provider you add, and points Claude Code at it. You pick the model in magpie or in Claude Code’s `/model`.

The gateway runs at `127.0.0.1:3425`. It speaks the Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini APIs. When a provider speaks Anthropic Messages itself, as DeepSeek, Kimi, Zhipu GLM, MiniMax and Qwen do, Claude Code’s request is passed on as it is. When it doesn’t, as with a GPT model from your ChatGPT plan, magpie translates the request and the reply, streaming and tool calls included.

### Chinese models

DeepSeek, Kimi and Kimi Code, Zhipu GLM (pay as you go or Coding Plan), Z.ai, MiniMax and Qwen, each with its China endpoint where it has one.

### Subscriptions

The models of a ChatGPT, Copilot or Antigravity account you sign in to in magpie.

### Anything else

Any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible URL and key, Ollama and LM Studio.

## Set it up

1. **Add the provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick DeepSeek, Kimi, Zhipu GLM, MiniMax or Qwen, paste your API key and save. magpie asks the vendor which models it serves.
2. **Pick the model for Claude Code.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the Claude Code row and choose one, such as `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`. magpie writes it into `~/.claude/settings.json`.
3. **Start a new session.** Claude Code reads its settings when it starts. A session already open keeps the model it started with.

The same from a terminal:

```
magpie provider add deepseek sk-…
magpie models                       # every model, as provider/model
magpie claude deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

Model ids are magpie’s, `provider/model`. Inside Claude Code, `/model` lists magpie’s models too, marked “via magpie”, so you can switch there.

> **Zhipu GLM Coding Plan.** When you add Zhipu GLM or Z.ai, pick the plan your key is for. A Coding Plan key has its own endpoints, and sent to the pay-as-you-go one it is told it has no balance.

> **Keep `claude` on your own account.** Leave Claude Code unconnected in magpie and run `claude-magpie` when you want it on another model. It starts the same `claude` with magpie’s settings for that session only, and `settings.json` is not rewritten. See [Get started](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/start#agents).

## How Opus, Sonnet and Haiku map

Claude Code asks for models by tier: `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku` and `fable`. Its own small jobs, such as a session’s title and Explore subagents, go to the haiku tier. magpie writes a model into each tier’s variable:

| Tier | Variable in `env` | By default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| opus | `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL` | The main model |
| sonnet | `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL` | The main model |
| haiku | `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL` | The main model; on a Claude model, the Haiku its provider serves |
| fable | `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL` | Left unset unless the main model is a Fable model |

So with DeepSeek as the main model, every tier runs on DeepSeek. To give a tier a model of its own, say a cheaper one for haiku, set it on the Claude Code row in magpie, or from a terminal:

```
magpie claude haiku deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash   # one tier on its own model
magpie claude haiku ""                           # back to the main model
```

A tier takes a model through magpie, and only once the main model is one.

## What changes in settings.json

Claude Code reads its endpoint from the `env` block of `~/.claude/settings.json`. magpie changes only the keys it needs there. Comments and your other settings stay.

| Key | Set to |
| --- | --- |
| `env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | The gateway’s address |
| `env.ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` | The gateway’s key (not your vendor key; that stays in magpie) |
| `model` | The main model |
| `env.ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL`, `env.ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL` | The tiers, as above |
| `env.CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | The longest reply the model can write. Claude Code asks a model it doesn’t know for 32000 at most |
| `env.CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS`, `env.CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` | Where needed, the model’s window and where to compact. Claude Code takes a model it doesn’t know for 200K. A 1M model is marked `[1m]` |
| `modelPicker` | magpie’s models, for `/model`. A picker you wrote yourself is left alone |

A value you set yourself, such as your own output limit, stays yours. `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` is taken out, because it would outrank a pick in `/model`. A cloud switch in that file, such as `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, is set aside while Claude Code runs through magpie and put back afterwards.

### Going back to Claude’s own models

Pick one of Claude Code’s own models on its row, or run `magpie claude default`. magpie takes out what it wrote and puts back what it replaced the first time: your own base URL, token and tier models. You don’t edit the file by hand.

## GPT models from a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription

Sign in to the subscription in magpie: ＋ Add provider, then the ChatGPT or Copilot tile. magpie opens the vendor’s own sign-in page. The account’s models then show in Claude Code’s picker as `codex/…` or `copilot/…`.

```
magpie accounts add codex      # sign in to a ChatGPT account
magpie claude codex/gpt-5.5
```

Claude Code still speaks Anthropic Messages. magpie translates each request for the GPT model and the reply back, tool calls included. Antigravity accounts work the same way, as `antigravity/…`. For a ChatGPT plan in full, tiers, effort and limits included, see [ChatGPT in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-chatgpt).

## Routing over several keys

With several keys or accounts, magpie can spread Claude Code’s requests over them and move on when one runs out.

- **Several keys for one vendor..** Add them all to the provider and tick each one. Routing on the provider says how requests spread, and Fallback lists models to use when it is out of quota or down.
- **One model from several providers..** When two of your providers serve the same model, such as DeepSeek from its own API and from a relay, magpie makes the group `auto/<model>` by itself. Pick it for Claude Code.
- **Your own group..** New group in the Routing tab puts any models behind one name, `group/<id>`.

The routing modes are in [Get started](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/start#routing).

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm) · [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/minimax) · [Anthropic](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/anthropic) · [OpenAI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openai) · [Gemini](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini) · [Grok](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/grok) · [Mistral](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/mistral) · [OpenRouter](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openrouter) · [GitHub Copilot](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/copilot) · [Ollama](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/ollama)

## FAQ

### Do I set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` myself?

No. magpie writes it into Claude Code’s `settings.json`. If `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX` or another cloud switch is set in your shell’s environment, Claude Code sends its requests to that cloud and not to magpie; magpie tells you so, and you take it out of your shell profile.

### Can I switch models inside Claude Code?

Yes. While Claude Code runs through magpie, `/model` lists magpie’s models and routing groups, and a pick there persists.

### Which Chinese models can Claude Code use?

Any that a provider you add serves. magpie has presets for DeepSeek, Kimi, Kimi Code, Zhipu GLM, Z.ai, MiniMax and Qwen, with China endpoints for Kimi, Kimi Code, MiniMax and Qwen. Others can be added as a custom URL.

### Does magpie have to be running?

Yes, while Claude Code is on a model through magpie: the gateway runs with the app. `magpie daemon install` keeps it running as a service with no window.

### Can I keep my claude.ai sign-in?

The Claude Code row has a sign-in setting. With magpie’s key, the default, Claude Code is signed out of claude.ai while it runs through magpie, so the plan limits in `/usage`, connectors, voice and `/teleport` are off. With claude.ai it keeps its sign-in, which magpie never passes on. Remote Control and ultrareview stay off either way.

### Can I use my Claude subscription and DeepSeek side by side?

Yes. Sign in to Claude in magpie and its models are `claude/…` in the same picker. Requests on a Claude subscription run through the Claude Code installed on your computer.

### How do I undo it?

Pick one of Claude Code’s own models in magpie, or run `magpie claude default`. What magpie wrote comes out, and what it replaced comes back.

Using Codex too? See [Use any model in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models). Stuck? Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models

# Use DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Claude or any model in Codex

Codex speaks one API, OpenAI Responses. magpie puts a gateway on your computer that speaks it for every provider you add, and writes Codex’s `config.toml` for you. The models then show in Codex’s `/model`, with their reasoning efforts.

The gateway runs at `127.0.0.1:3425`. When a provider serves the Responses API itself, as DeepSeek and the Zhipu GLM Coding Plan do, Codex’s request is passed on as it is. When it serves only Chat Completions or Anthropic Messages, as Kimi, MiniMax and Qwen do, or a Claude subscription, magpie translates the request and the reply, streaming and tool calls included.

### Chinese models

DeepSeek, Kimi and Kimi Code, Zhipu GLM (pay as you go or Coding Plan), Z.ai, MiniMax and Qwen, each with its China endpoint where it has one.

### Claude

Your Claude subscription’s models, or an Anthropic key’s.

### Anything else

Any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible URL and key, Copilot and Antigravity accounts, Ollama and LM Studio.

## Set it up

1. **Add the provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick DeepSeek, Kimi, Zhipu GLM, MiniMax or Qwen, paste your API key and save. magpie asks the vendor which models it serves.
2. **Pick the model for Codex.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the Codex row and choose one, such as `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`. The effort slider under the list sets its reasoning effort. magpie writes both into `~/.codex/config.toml`.
3. **Restart Codex.** Codex builds its model list when it starts. Restart the Codex app, and open new `codex` sessions, after a switch.

The same from a terminal:

```
magpie provider add deepseek sk-…
magpie models                        # every model, as provider/model
magpie codex deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
magpie codex effort high
```

> **Zhipu GLM Coding Plan.** When you add Zhipu GLM or Z.ai, pick the plan your key is for. A Coding Plan key has its own endpoints, and sent to the pay-as-you-go one it is told it has no balance.

## The models in Codex’s /model

magpie’s models are listed in Codex’s `/model` beside its own, so you can switch there too. Each one carries what Codex needs to run it: its reasoning efforts and default effort, its context window and the base instructions Codex sends with it.

How they get there depends on how Codex is signed in:

- **Signed in to ChatGPT..** Codex keeps its own OpenAI provider and your sign-in. magpie points it at the gateway with `openai_base_url`; Codex’s own models still go to OpenAI on your account, and magpie’s models join them in `/model`.
- **Not signed in, or signed in with an API key..** magpie becomes Codex’s provider, and the list comes from a catalog file magpie writes, `magpie-models.json` beside `config.toml`.

## What changes in config.toml

magpie changes only the keys it needs in `~/.codex/config.toml`. Comments, ordering and your other settings stay.

| Key | Set to |
| --- | --- |
| `model` | The model you picked |
| `model_reasoning_effort` | The effort, when you set one |
| `openai_base_url` | The gateway’s address. A base URL of your own stays |
| `model_provider` | `"magpie"`, when magpie is the provider |
| `model_catalog_json` | The path of the catalog file, `magpie-models.json`, when magpie is the provider |
| `[model_providers.magpie]` | `name`, `base_url` (the gateway’s `/v1`), `wire_api = "responses"`, and the gateway’s key. Your vendor keys stay in magpie |

```
model = "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"
model_provider = "magpie"
model_catalog_json = "/Users/you/.codex/magpie-models.json"

[model_providers.magpie]
name = "magpie"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1"
wire_api = "responses"
```

That is the shape when magpie is the provider; the table also carries the gateway’s key and a header. Signed in to ChatGPT, only `openai_base_url` and `model` are set at the top. The `[model_providers.magpie]` table stays once written. A Codex thread keeps the provider it was started on, and a thread started on magpie can’t be opened again without it.

### Going back to OpenAI’s models

Pick one of Codex’s own models on its row, or run `magpie codex default`. magpie takes `model_provider`, `model_catalog_json` and the base URL back out and puts back the provider and model you had. A provider of your own at the top stays. Threads started on magpie are moved back to the provider Codex is on, so Codex lists them, and a copy is kept in magpie’s trash.

## Claude in Codex

Sign in to your Claude subscription in magpie: ＋ Add provider, then the Claude tile. Its models are `claude/…` in Codex’s picker. magpie translates Codex’s Responses requests into Anthropic Messages and the replies back.

```
magpie accounts add claude     # sign in to a Claude account
magpie models | grep '^claude/'
magpie codex claude/…
```

Requests on a Claude subscription run through the Claude Code installed on your computer, so keep it installed. An Anthropic API key works too: add Anthropic as a vendor and pick an `anthropic/…` model.

## Routing over several keys

- **Several keys for one vendor..** Add them all to the provider and tick each one. Routing on the provider says how requests spread, and Fallback lists models to use when it is out of quota or down.
- **One model from several providers..** When two of your providers serve the same model, magpie makes the group `auto/<model>` by itself. Pick it for Codex.
- **Your own group..** New group in the Routing tab puts any models behind one name, `group/<id>`.

The routing modes are in [Get started](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/start#routing).

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm) · [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/minimax) · [Anthropic](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/anthropic) · [OpenAI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openai) · [Gemini](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini) · [Grok](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/grok) · [Mistral](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/mistral) · [OpenRouter](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openrouter) · [GitHub Copilot](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/copilot) · [Ollama](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/ollama)

## FAQ

### Do I write `[model_providers]` myself?

No. magpie writes Codex’s `config.toml` when you pick a model. You don’t export `OPENAI_BASE_URL` either.

### Does my ChatGPT sign-in still work?

Yes. Signed in to ChatGPT, Codex keeps its own provider and sign-in. Its own models go to OpenAI on your account, and magpie’s are added beside them.

### I picked a model, but Codex’s /model doesn’t show it.

Codex reads its model list when it starts. Restart the Codex app and open a new `codex` session.

### Can I set the reasoning effort?

Yes, on the Codex row’s effort slider, with `magpie codex effort high`, or in Codex’s `/model`, which lists each model’s efforts.

### Which Chinese models can Codex use?

Any that a provider you add serves. magpie has presets for DeepSeek, Kimi, Kimi Code, Zhipu GLM, Z.ai, MiniMax and Qwen. Others can be added as a custom URL.

### Does magpie have to be running?

Yes, while Codex is on a model through magpie: the gateway runs with the app. `magpie daemon install` keeps it running as a service with no window.

### How do I undo it?

Pick one of Codex’s own models in magpie, or run `magpie codex default`. magpie’s keys come out, and your provider and model come back.

Using Claude Code too? See [Use any model in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models). Stuck? Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models

# Use DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Claude or GPT in Gemini CLI

Gemini CLI speaks only Google’s Gemini API. magpie puts a gateway on your computer that serves the Gemini API for every provider you add, and points Gemini CLI at it. You pick the model on Gemini CLI’s row in magpie.

The gateway runs at `127.0.0.1:3425`. It serves the Gemini API’s `generateContent`, `streamGenerateContent` and `countTokens` calls and its model list, beside the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs. A request goes straight through when the provider speaks the Gemini API, and is translated when it doesn’t, as with DeepSeek, Kimi, Zhipu GLM or a Claude or ChatGPT subscription: the request and the reply, streaming, tool calls, images and reasoning included.

### Chinese models

DeepSeek, Kimi and Kimi Code, Zhipu GLM (pay as you go or Coding Plan), Z.ai, MiniMax and Qwen.

### Subscriptions

The models of a Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot or Antigravity account you sign in to in magpie.

### Anything else

Any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible URL and key, Ollama and LM Studio.

## Set it up

1. **Add the provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick DeepSeek, Kimi, Zhipu GLM, MiniMax or Qwen, paste your API key and save. magpie asks the vendor which models it serves.
2. **Pick the model for Gemini CLI.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the Gemini CLI row and choose one, such as `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`. magpie writes it into `~/.gemini/settings.json` and the gateway’s address into `~/.gemini/.env`.
3. **Restart gemini.** Gemini CLI reads its settings when it starts. A session already open keeps what it started with.

The same from a terminal:

```
magpie provider add deepseek sk-…
magpie models                              # every model, as provider/model
magpie gemini model deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

Model ids are magpie’s, `provider/model`. The Gemini CLI row shows once the `gemini` command is on your `PATH`.

> **Zhipu GLM Coding Plan.** When you add Zhipu GLM or Z.ai, pick the plan your key is for. A Coding Plan key has its own endpoints, and sent to the pay-as-you-go one it is told it has no balance.

## What changes in ~/.gemini

Gemini CLI loads `~/.gemini/.env` and reads `~/.gemini/settings.json`. magpie changes four keys across the two:

| File | Key | Set to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.env` | `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` | The gateway’s address |
| `.env` | `GEMINI_API_KEY` | The gateway’s key (not your vendor key; that stays in magpie) |
| `settings.json` | `security.auth.selectedType` | `gemini-api-key`, so Gemini CLI sends that key and not a Google sign-in |
| `settings.json` | `model.name` | The model, as `provider/model` |

The first time, magpie keeps what those keys held before: your own base URL, API key, sign-in choice and model. If the sign-in choice is changed to anything but the API key while the model is one of magpie’s, Gemini CLI asks Google directly, and magpie’s Gemini CLI row says so.

### Going back to Google

Pick one of Gemini CLI’s own Gemini models on its row, or run `magpie gemini default`. magpie takes `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` and `GEMINI_API_KEY` out of `.env` and puts back the base URL, key, sign-in choice and model you had. You don’t edit either file by hand.

The row’s auth setting chooses how Gemini CLI signs in on its own: Google (your Google account), API key or Vertex AI. With Google Gemini added as a provider in magpie, API key writes that key into `.env` for Gemini CLI.

```
magpie gemini default   # magpie’s wiring out, what you had back
magpie gemini google    # sign in with your Google account
```

## Claude and GPT models from a subscription

Sign in to the subscription in magpie: ＋ Add provider, then the Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot tile. magpie opens the vendor’s own sign-in page. The account’s models are then `claude/…`, `codex/…` or `copilot/…` on Gemini CLI’s row.

```
magpie accounts add codex           # sign in to a ChatGPT account
magpie gemini model codex/gpt-5.5
```

Gemini CLI still speaks the Gemini API; magpie translates each request for the model and the reply back. Requests on a Claude subscription run through the Claude Code installed on your computer, so keep it installed. More in [Use your subscription in any agent](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/subscriptions).

## Routing over several keys

- **Several keys for one vendor..** Add them all to the provider and tick each one. Routing on the provider says how requests spread, and Fallback lists models to use when it is out of quota or down.
- **One model from several providers..** When two of your providers serve the same model, magpie makes the group `auto/<model>` by itself. Pick it for Gemini CLI.
- **A cheaper model for compaction..** A routing group’s compacting rule matches Gemini CLI compacting its conversation, so a cheaper, faster model can write the summary.

The routing modes and rules are in [Get started](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/start#routing).

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm) · [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/minimax) · [Anthropic](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/anthropic) · [OpenAI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openai) · [Gemini](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini) · [Grok](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/grok) · [Mistral](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/mistral) · [OpenRouter](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openrouter) · [GitHub Copilot](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/copilot) · [Ollama](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/ollama)

## FAQ

### Can Gemini CLI use models that aren’t Gemini?

Yes, through a gateway that serves the Gemini API. magpie runs one on your computer and points Gemini CLI at it, so any model of a provider you add works: DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Qwen, MiniMax, or a Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

### Do I set `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` myself?

No. magpie writes it and `GEMINI_API_KEY` into `~/.gemini/.env`, and sets Gemini CLI to API-key auth in `~/.gemini/settings.json`. What you had there before is kept and comes back when you switch away.

### Why does Gemini CLI still send requests to Google?

Its sign-in choice is not the API key: with a Google sign-in or Vertex AI, Gemini CLI asks Google directly. Pick the model again in magpie, which sets it back to the API key; magpie’s Gemini CLI row tells you when this happens. Restart open `gemini` sessions after a change.

### Can I use my ChatGPT or Claude subscription in Gemini CLI?

Yes. Sign in to it in magpie and pick a `codex/…` or `claude/…` model on Gemini CLI’s row. Requests on a Claude subscription run through the Claude Code installed on your computer.

### Why doesn’t magpie show Gemini CLI?

magpie shows it when the `gemini` command is on your `PATH`. A `~/.gemini` folder alone doesn’t count, because it stays after Gemini CLI is uninstalled and Antigravity keeps folders there too.

### Does it work for Gemini CLI in WSL?

Yes. magpie sets up Gemini CLI inside a WSL distro the same way, writing the gateway’s address as that distro reaches it.

### How do I switch Gemini CLI back to Google?

Pick one of Gemini CLI’s own models in magpie, or run `magpie gemini default`. What magpie wrote comes out, and your own key, sign-in choice and model come back.

Using Claude Code or Codex too? See [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models) and [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models). Stuck? Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/subscriptions

# Use your Claude Pro/Max, ChatGPT Plus/Pro or GitHub Copilot subscription in any coding agent

Sign in to a subscription once, in magpie. Its models then show in every agent magpie sets up: GPT models from your ChatGPT plan in Claude Code, Claude models from your Claude plan in Codex or OpenCode, Copilot’s models in any of them. No API key.

magpie runs a gateway on your computer, at `127.0.0.1:3425`. It speaks the OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini APIs and translates between them, streaming and tool calls included, so an agent that speaks one API can use a model served in another. magpie writes the gateway’s address and key into each agent’s own config file.

## Which subscriptions

| Subscription | Models are | Sign in from a terminal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude (Pro, Max, Team) | `claude/…` | `magpie accounts add claude` |
| ChatGPT (Plus, Pro, Business) | `codex/…` | `magpie accounts add codex` |
| GitHub Copilot | `copilot/…` | `magpie accounts add copilot` |
| Gemini (Code Assist) | `gemini/…` | `magpie accounts add gemini` |
| Antigravity | `antigravity/…` | `magpie accounts add antigravity` |

- **Claude..** Requests on a Claude subscription run through the Claude Code installed on your computer, so keep it installed.
- **Copilot..** Copilot gives you a code to enter on GitHub’s page. For GitHub Enterprise on its own domain: `magpie accounts add copilot --host <name>.ghe.com`.
- **Gemini..** This is Gemini CLI’s Google sign-in. Google answers it only for a Code Assist Standard or Enterprise account with a Google Cloud project of its own; `magpie accounts project gemini <email> <project>` names the project.
- **Antigravity..** Its sign-in gives Antigravity’s Claude and Gemini models.

Other subscriptions are added as plugins, from magpie’s Plugins page; see [Plugins](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/plugins).

## Sign in

1. **Open Add provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider.
2. **Click the subscription’s tile.** magpie opens the vendor’s own sign-in page in your browser. The account shows up as soon as you finish.
3. **Pick its model for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose one of the subscription’s models.

An agent you are already signed in to on this machine, such as Claude Code or Codex, shows up as a provider too, *signed in as …*. `magpie accounts discovery off` stops magpie reading those sign-ins.

## Use it in another agent

A subscription’s models are in every agent’s picker in magpie. A few pairs people ask for:

| Agent | Subscription | From a terminal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | ChatGPT | `magpie claude codex/gpt-5.5` |
| Codex | Claude | `magpie codex claude/claude-opus-5-5` |
| Gemini CLI | ChatGPT | `magpie gemini model codex/gpt-5.5` |
| OpenCode | Claude | Pick a `claude/…` model on OpenCode’s row |

`magpie models` lists every model you can pick, as `provider/model`. Each agent’s guide says what magpie changes in its config and how to undo it: [Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models), [Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models). `magpie <agent> default` takes magpie’s wiring out of an agent and puts back what it had.

## Several accounts and failover

- **Add another account..** Click the Claude or ChatGPT tile again, or run `magpie accounts add` again. Each account is listed under the provider.
- **Spread requests over them..** Open the provider’s row and tick every account to use. Routing says how requests spread: Smart, the default, sends them to the account with quota to spare whose allowance renews soonest; In order, Until used up, In turn, Least used first, Use before expiry, By weight (a Max account 5, a Pro one 1) and Speed first are the others.
- **Fall back when they run out..** The provider’s Fallback lists models to use when it is out of quota, rate limited or down.
- **One model on two subscriptions..** Claude Opus from your Claude subscription and from Copilot become one group by themselves, `auto/<model>`. Pick it to use both.
- **See what’s left..** `magpie accounts` lists each account and how much of its allowance is used.

The routing modes are in [Get started](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/start#routing).

## Other tools

Any tool with a base-URL setting can use a subscription through the gateway too. The Gateway tab’s Connect section has the address and key to copy. The base URL is `http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1` for an OpenAI client and `http://127.0.0.1:3425` for an Anthropic or Gemini one. See [Integrate your app](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/integrate).

## FAQ

### Can I use my ChatGPT Plus or Pro subscription in Claude Code?

Yes. Sign in to ChatGPT in magpie and pick a `codex/…` model on Claude Code’s row, or run `magpie claude codex/gpt-5.5`. magpie translates Claude Code’s Anthropic requests for the GPT model and the replies back, tool calls included. The whole setup, tiers and effort included, is in [ChatGPT in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-chatgpt).

### Can I use my Claude Pro or Max subscription in Codex or OpenCode?

Yes. Sign in to Claude in magpie and pick a `claude/…` model on the agent’s row. Requests on a Claude subscription run through the Claude Code installed on your computer, so keep it installed.

### Can I use GitHub Copilot models outside VS Code?

Yes. Sign in to Copilot in magpie (GitHub gives you a code to enter), and its models are `copilot/…` in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and the other agents magpie sets up.

### Do I need an API key to use a subscription in another agent?

No. magpie signs in on the vendor’s own page and the agent gets the gateway’s key. Your sign-in stays in magpie.

### Can I use several Claude or ChatGPT accounts and switch when one hits its limit?

Yes. Add each account in magpie and tick them on the provider’s row. Smart routing, the default, uses an account with quota to spare, and moves on when one is out or rate limited. `magpie accounts` shows what each has left.

### Do my requests go through a magpie server?

No. The gateway runs on your computer. Your prompts, replies, keys and accounts go only to the providers you use; magpie has no server of its own in that path.

### Does each agent have to be signed in to the subscription?

No. Subscriptions are added in magpie, not by signing in inside another agent. One sign-in serves every agent you point at it.

Using a key instead? See [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models) and [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models). Stuck? Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-chatgpt

# Use your ChatGPT Plus or Pro subscription in Claude Code

Claude Code can run on the GPT models of your ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan. Sign in to ChatGPT in magpie, pick a `codex/…` model for Claude Code, and keep working as before. No OpenAI API key.

Claude Code speaks Anthropic’s Messages API. magpie runs a gateway on your computer, at `127.0.0.1:3425`, that translates each of Claude Code’s requests for the GPT model and each reply back, streaming and tool calls included. magpie writes the gateway’s address and key into Claude Code’s `settings.json`, and your ChatGPT sign-in stays in magpie.

## Sign in to ChatGPT

1. **Open Add provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider.
2. **Click the ChatGPT tile.** magpie opens OpenAI’s own sign-in page in your browser. The account shows up as soon as you finish.

Or from a terminal:

```
magpie accounts add codex      # sign in to a ChatGPT account
```

The account’s models are `codex/…`.

## Pick a GPT model for Claude Code

In the Agents tab, click the model on Claude Code’s row and choose a `codex/…` model. From a terminal:

```
magpie models                  # every model, as provider/model
magpie claude codex/gpt-5.5
```

Inside Claude Code, `/model` lists magpie’s models too, marked “via magpie”, so you can switch there.

> **Only some sessions on GPT?** Leave Claude Code unconnected in magpie and run `claude-magpie` when you want it on a GPT model. It starts the same `claude` with magpie’s settings for that session only, and `settings.json` is not rewritten.

## How Opus, Sonnet and Haiku map

Claude Code asks for models by tier: `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku` and `fable`. Its own small jobs, such as a session’s title and Explore subagents, go to the haiku tier. With a GPT model as the main model:

| Tier | Variable in `env` | By default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| opus | `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL` | The GPT model you picked |
| sonnet | `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL` | The GPT model you picked |
| haiku | `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL` | The GPT model you picked |
| fable | `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL` | Left unset |

To give a tier a model of its own, say a smaller one for haiku, set it on Claude Code’s row in magpie, or from a terminal:

```
magpie claude haiku codex/…    # one tier on its own model
magpie claude haiku ""         # back to the main model
```

## Reasoning effort

The effort Claude Code asks for goes to the GPT model as its reasoning effort, on requests where Claude Code has thinking on. magpie also tells Claude Code which effort levels each model has.

To hold one effort whatever Claude Code asks, set effort on Claude Code’s row. opus effort, sonnet effort, haiku effort, fable effort and subagent effort set it per tier. Each starts at the effort Claude Code asks for. An open Claude Code session keeps the effort it started with, so restart it to use a new one.

## Limits and usage

Requests are served on your ChatGPT account, so they count toward your plan’s usage limits, as Codex’s own requests do.

- **See what’s used..** Turn on status line on Claude Code’s row: it shows the 5h and 7d use of the accounts magpie serves, under Claude Code’s prompt. `magpie accounts` lists each account and how much of its allowance is used. The Usage tab has the history.
- **When an account runs out..** magpie sets it aside until the reset OpenAI’s refusal names, else until its full window renews, else for 5 hours, and sends requests to your next account or the provider’s Fallback. The account comes back on its own once its window renews.

## Several accounts and failover

- **Add another account..** Click the ChatGPT tile again, or run `magpie accounts add codex` again. Each account is listed under the provider.
- **Spread requests over them..** Open the provider’s row and tick every account to use. Smart routing, the default, sends requests to the account with quota to spare whose allowance renews soonest.
- **Fall back to another model..** The provider’s Fallback lists models to use when every account is out, rate limited or down, a model from another subscription or an API key included.

The routing modes are in [Get started](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/start#routing).

## Switch back

Pick one of Claude Code’s own models on its row, or run:

```
magpie claude default
```

That takes magpie’s wiring out of Claude Code and puts back what it had. Disconnect on Claude Code’s row does the same.

> **Your claude.ai sign-in.** On a magpie model, Claude Code’s sign-in setting is magpie’s key by default: claude.ai is signed out for it, so `/usage` plan limits, connectors, voice and `/teleport` are off. Set it to claude.ai to keep them.

## The other way round: Claude in Codex

A Claude Pro or Max subscription works in Codex the same way. Sign in to Claude in magpie and pick a `claude/…` model for Codex. Requests on a Claude subscription run through the Claude Code installed on your computer, so keep it installed.

```
magpie accounts add claude
magpie codex claude/claude-opus-5-5
```

See [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models) and [Subscriptions in any agent](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/subscriptions).

## FAQ

### Can I use my ChatGPT Plus or Pro subscription in Claude Code?

Yes. Sign in to ChatGPT in magpie and pick a `codex/…` model on Claude Code’s row, or run `magpie claude codex/gpt-5.5`. magpie translates Claude Code’s requests for the GPT model and the replies back, tool calls included.

### Do I need an OpenAI API key?

No. magpie signs in on OpenAI’s own page, and Claude Code gets the gateway’s key. Your sign-in stays in magpie.

### Does it use my ChatGPT plan’s limits?

Yes. Requests are served on your ChatGPT account and count toward its usage limits. magpie’s status line shows each account’s 5h and 7d use under Claude Code’s prompt.

### Which model do Claude Code’s Haiku requests use?

The GPT model you picked, unless you give the haiku tier a model of its own with `magpie claude haiku <model>`.

### How do I go back to Claude’s own models?

Run `magpie claude default`, or pick one of Claude Code’s own models on its row in magpie.

### Do my requests go through a magpie server?

No. The gateway runs on your computer. Requests go from it to OpenAI; magpie has no server of its own in that path.

Using an API key instead? See [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).
